claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch on the current record because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and the fraud dispute review gap is only an unresolved disclosure/materiality issue rather than a blocker to certification.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case.
Non-core or low-volume product labels do not resolve materiality when the segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
Material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Public governance principles can support monitoring practices but do not override the specific release policy predicate.
evidence_requests: Approved risk acceptance explicitly covering the fraud dispute review gap before launch.
Final legal determination on whether the gap must be disclosed for the named bank pilot commitments.
The actual launch disclosure or model-card text showing the material limitation has been documented for the named use case.
Evidence that the named bank pilot commitments are not contractual customer commitments or not part of the named launch use case.
Updated evaluation results showing the fraud dispute review segment no longer misses target.
specific_concerns: The admissible record shows a named segment evaluation gap: the fraud dispute review segment misses target by 1.3 percentage points and is named in two bank pilot commitments.
The governing policy says material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The policy text further says product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the affected segment is named in customer commitments or when legal review is pending.
Legal review is still open, with no final answer on whether the gap must be disclosed.
There is no admissible evidence of disclosure, resolution of the gap, or approved risk acceptance, so a required policy predicate for certification is missing.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not negate a material named-use-case limitation under the stated policy.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently supportable on the current record despite the unresolved named-use-case gap.
That the issue is merely a disclosure caveat rather than a potential certification blocker.
That the 7% projected first-month traffic argument resolves materiality; admissible evidence says it does not, and it does not address the two named bank pilot commitments.
That public governance guidance permitting deployment with monitoring is sufficient support for this release decision under the specific internal policy.
